subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the essential elements required to form a legally binding contract?
questions.explain: The core elements of a valid contract are Offer, Acceptance, Consideration, Competent Parties, and Legal Purpose. Notarization is not a strict requirement for a basic contract to be legally binding.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

options: The mutual understanding of the contract terms by both parties.
Something of legal value exchanged between the parties.
The time allowed for a buyer to review goods upon delivery.
A thoughtful review of the contract by legal counsel.
questions.explain: Consideration is the bargained-for exchange of value between parties to a contract (e.g., money exchanged for goods or services). Without consideration, a promise is generally a non-binding gift.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A public agency issues an Invitation for Bids (IFB). Under common law contract principles, the issuance of the IFB is legally considered:
options: A request for offers (invitation to treat)
questions.explain: Solicitations like an IFB or RFP are legally categorized as 'invitations to treat' or a request for offers. The bid submitted by the vendor is the actual 'Offer' that the agency may then choose to accept.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Vendor A submits an offer to sell 100 laptops for $50,000. The purchasing agent responds: 'We agree to buy 100 laptops, but only for $45,000.' In contract law, the agent's response is classified as a(n):
questions.explain: A counteroffer occurs when the offeree materially alters the terms of the original offer. A counteroffer simultaneously rejects the original offer and creates a new one.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: To be enforceable, certain types of contracts—such as contracts for the sale of goods over $500, or contracts that cannot be performed within one year—must be in writing. This legal principle is known as:
questions.explain: The Statute of Frauds requires certain types of contracts to be memorialized in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought to be legally binding.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A contract that involves purchasing stolen property lacks which essential element, thereby rendering it unenforceable?
questions.explain: A contract must have a Legal Purpose. Agreements to perform illegal acts, such as trafficking stolen goods, are void because they lack a legal purpose.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: What is the difference between a void contract and a voidable contract?
options: A void contract is lacking an element and was never legally valid; a voidable contract is valid but can be affirmed or rejected at the option of one party.
A void contract can be canceled by mutual consent; a voidable contract can only be canceled by a judge.
Void contracts involve goods; voidable contracts involve services.
There is no difference; the terms are synonymous in contract law.
questions.explain: A void contract has no legal effect from inception (e.g., illegal purpose). A voidable contract is one where one party has the right to either escape the contract or enforce it (e.g., a contract signed by a minor).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When assessing 'Mutual Assent' (or a meeting of the minds) during contract formation, courts generally look at:
options: The secret, subjective intent of the purchasing agent.
The objective manifestations of intent by both parties, such as words and conduct.
The financial status of the vendor.
The length of time it took to draft the solicitation.
questions.explain: Mutual assent is judged objectively by what the parties said and did (their outward manifestations), rather than what they secretly intended.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: In public procurement, a bidder's capacity to legally enter into a contract involves analyzing whether the entity is legally authorized to do business and whether the signatory has the right to bind the company. This evaluates which contract element?
questions.explain: 'Competent Parties' refers to the legal capacity of both parties to enter into an agreement, which includes age, mental capacity, and the actual corporate authority to bind a business entity.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: What does a 'breach of contract' fundamentally entail?
options: The expiration of a contract term without renewal.
A mutual agreement to terminate performance.
The failure of a party to perform an obligation defined in the contract without legal excuse.
The invocation of a force majeure clause due to an act of God.
questions.explain: A breach of contract is an unexcused failure to perform any promise that forms all or part of the contract.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: An agency mails a formal purchase order (an offer) to a supplier. The supplier begins manufacturing and shipping the goods as described in the PO without formally signing and returning the document. Under contract law, shipping the goods constitutes:
options: A breach of the Perfect Tender Rule
questions.explain: An offer can often be accepted by promising to perform or by actual performance. By beginning to ship the requested goods, the supplier manifests acceptance of the agency's offer.
